speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your symptoms, can you tell me if the double vision and weakness have been getting progressively worse over time, or did they appear suddenly? Also, do you have any difficulty swallowing or speaking?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: That pattern of fluctuating weakness that improves with rest is very significant. Do you have any ptosis (drooping eyelids) or does your facial weakness change throughout the day?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for that information. To confirm the diagnosis, I need to check for specific signs. Can you look straight ahead and then try to look up without moving your head? Does your upper eyelid droop or cover your pupil when you do this?

REQUEST TEST: Acetylcholine_Receptor_Antibody_Test

speaker: Doctor
text:
The elevated Acetylcholine Receptor Antibody test confirms the diagnosis of Myasthenia Gravis.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis
